# Test

<!-- Generated by `prism docs` from `lib/std/Test.pr`. Do not edit by hand. -->

Test assertions and per-type value generators for property testing.

`fail_with`, `expect`, `expect_equal`, and `expect_text` fail the running `test fn` with a structured payload: a message, and for `expect_equal` the expected and actual values with a line diff between them. The payload travels to `prism test` as the versioned `prism-test-failure-v1` envelope, written as the test's last output line just before the failure fires, and the runner reports its fields in place of a bare `test failed`.

A generator is the unwrapped `Quickcheck.Gen`: a size-bounded draw from the ambient `Random` capability. That makes a run deterministic under a seed (the `Quickcheck` runner serves `Random` from a seeded SplitMix64 stream), and lets a derived instance recurse through its fields' `arbitrary` while composing cleanly with the `Gen` combinators. The primitive instances delegate to `Quickcheck`'s canonical generators, so a derived type draws from the same distributions the hand-written harness does.

Wrap an instance back into a `Gen` with `arb_gen` to feed it to `quickcheck`.

## Type Classes

### `Arbitrary`

```prism,def,h-b8174e0edc77c1de535e66e7a36e1cf43d2ece66f95c68f9d563dd552f586eb7
class Arbitrary(a)
  arbitrary : (Int) -> a ! {Random | e}
```

A structural generator, sized by a fuel budget. `deriving (Arbitrary)` spends the budget on depth: at each recursive constructor it draws its fields a size smaller, and once the budget runs out it restricts to non-recursive constructors, so generation always terminates.

## Functions and Values

### `fail_with`

```prism,sig,h-65f430fe5da336720e306f83e45215d26faf8374330ebfa2e3b1d643e0cf5689
fail_with : forall a. (String) -> a ! {Fail, Output}
```

Fail the running test with `message`.

```prism,no_run,mod=Test
test fn parses() =
  match parse_int("12") of
    Some(_) => ()
    None => fail_with("`12` did not parse")
```

### `expect`

```prism,sig,h-8ae804a532f135de3d5e6b4039bdd7697ade2870274666de6b06ccec2e5886ca
expect : (Bool, String) -> Unit ! {Fail, Output}
```

Fail the running test with `message` unless `cond` holds.

### `expect_equal`

```prism,sig,h-f1539315d0d2bb86ca2ac363efbd958a34f67172583147305320a962043c84ac
expect_equal : forall a. (a, a) -> Unit ! {Fail, Output} given Eq(a), Show(a)
```

Fail the running test unless `actual` equals `expected`, reporting both values and a line diff between their renderings.

```prism,no_run,mod=Test
test fn adds() = expect_equal(4, 2 + 2)
```

### `expect_text`

```prism,sig,h-11d8bfe47942b43791e2e702c9545527ed0ff770117f643f0ef9079eeae394be
expect_text : (String, String) -> Unit ! {Fail, Output}
```

Fail the running test unless the text `actual` equals `expected`, reporting a line diff of the raw text. Prefer this to `expect_equal` for multi-line strings, whose `Show` rendering escapes the line breaks a diff needs.

### `arb_gen`

```prism,sig,h-1a5e6613b0a4226d4bf4a4db2bc8e03b3ffd252ae767d3c7a13c69669ffa8e7c
arb_gen : forall a. () -> Quickcheck.Gen(a) given Test.Arbitrary(a)
```

The generator of an `Arbitrary` type, as a `Quickcheck.Gen` ready for `quickcheck`/`gen_at`.

```prism,no_run,mod=Test
# import Quickcheck (..)
fn prop(xs : List(Int)) : Bool = reverse(reverse(xs)) == xs

fn main() = println(passed(quickcheck(arb_gen(), prop)))
```
